newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan may send food to N.Korea if Seoul asks-Kyodo.
newsitem.headline: Japan may send food to N.Korea if Seoul asks-Kyodo.

text.p: Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Thursday that Japan may extend emergency food aid to North Korea if the South Korean government makes a formal request for it to do so, Kyodo news service reported.

"If the South Korean government asks us for assistance to compatriots in North Korea, there is room for the Japanese side to change its stance (on giving food aid)," Kyodo quoted Hashimoto as telling a group of visiting South Korean newspaper editors.
Japan has refused to provide food aid to famine-stricken North Korea, accusing the Pyongyang government of a string of kidnappings of Japanese citizens in the 1970s and drug smuggling.
Tokyo has also demanded that Pyongyang allow Japanese wives of Koreans living in North Korea to visit their homeland.

"There is the problem of Japanese wives, and allegations that 10 Japanese have been kidnapped in addition to the alleged abduction of a teenage schoolgirl and suspicions about stimulant smuggling," Kyodo quoted Hashimoto as telling the editors.
"We are ready to think about that (food aid) if we are asked to render aid by the South Korean government. Anyhow, we will have inter-governmental consultations," Kyodo quoted Hashimoto as saying.
